title: On-call Copilot
description: Walk through evidence-grounded incident triage on recorded runbooks and past incidents, then adapt the same gate to your corpus, with wrong-person refusal, expiry without auto-approval, a closed action registry, and a complete audit trail.

preview.alt: On-call Copilot triaging an alert with evidence and an approval gate
preview.caption: Evidence-ranked triage with a human approval gate before action.

run.url: the Local URL printed by the server

prerequisites: Optional live adaptation: a Glean instance with a service catalog, runbooks, and incident reviews, plus a work email for OAuth sign-in or a scoped API token

demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The fixture-backed copilot acknowledges in the channel, resolves the service to its on-call engineer and owner from the recorded catalog, fans out retrieval, and posts a triage card. A matching past incident supports the probable cause; the runbook supports the proposed action.

demoQueries.query: Triage an alert with no matching past incident
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The highest-scoring retrieved document will often be a runbook, so a relevance-ranked copilot would confidently blame whatever that runbook is about. With no matching signature and nothing in flight, this copilot asserts no cause. Ranking is not evidence.

demoQueries.query: Approve the proposed action as someone who is not on call
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Choose the outsider under Acting as, then approve. The gate refuses the request with 403 and audits it against that actor. The allowed set is the on-call engineer and service owner read from the recorded service catalog. The incident stays awaiting approval.

The proposal escalates to the target named in the recorded service catalog and is NOT executed. Auto-approving on timeout would invert the point of a gate. The escalation is audited and posted to the channel.

demoQueries.query: Have the Glean agent propose an action that is not registered
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Click Off-script agent · PAY-2233. The action is refused at proposal time and audited, with no approval card offered. An agent that can describe arbitrary actions into existence has production access, whatever its prompt says.

steps.title: Watch the governance hold, with no credentials
steps.description: Replays recorded responses and asserts the parts that matter: the gate refuses the wrong actor, expiry escalates without executing, an unregistered action is refused, a mutating action with no supported cause is downgraded, and every attempt is audited.

steps.title: Exercise the gate
steps.description: Fire all three sample alarms. Confirm the first cause cites a past incident, the second asserts no cause and offers an investigation ticket, the off-script agent action is refused before an approval card appears, choosing the outsider under Acting as produces an audited 403, and forcing expiry escalates without execution.

aiPrompt: Build the On-call Copilot following the oncall-copilot recipe. Start with the recorded fixtures; they are the supported demo path. Only a matching past incident may support a cause, while a runbook may support a procedure. Do not offer a code-changing action without a supported cause. Gate actions behind authorized human approval, expiry, a closed action registry, and an audit log. The acting user is asserted, not authenticated. Actions are simulated in-process. Treat live mode as a corpus adaptation that requires changing the catalog query, parser, identity mapping, and evidence URL rules.
llmContext: Use the recorded Search, Chat, and Agent responses for the default run. The app runs as the caller, so its approval check is application policy, not impersonation. Classify precedent from /incidents/ and procedure from /runbooks/ in URLs. Only a matching past incident may support a cause. A mutating action needs a supported cause, an authorized approver, a registered action id, and an unexpired proposal. Unauthorized approvals, executions, and expirations are audited. Registered actions are in-process simulations. Fixture mode permits actor assertion so the dashboard can demonstrate the 403. Live mode refuses it unless INCIDENT_DEMO_MODE is true. Do not claim that npm run start:live works against an arbitrary Glean corpus without adapting the parsers.

codeAssets.description: Webhook, service registry, retrieval fan-out, evidence classification, triage card, approval gate, pre-registered actions, and a postmortem timeline. Both orchestrators render into one shell.

content.problem:
An alarm fires at 3am. The runbook, the review of the last time this happened, who owns the service, and what it depends on all exist in Glean already. They just sit in different systems, and you search them one at a time while the graphs get worse.

The retrieval is the easy part. What makes a copilot safe to point at a production service is what it refuses to do, so that is what you build here. The gate turns away anyone who is not on call. A proposal nobody approves in time escalates instead of quietly approving itself. An action the planner invented never reaches a human. Every attempt lands in the audit log, including the refused ones.

Know the edges before you point it anywhere real. Live Search, Chat, and optional Agents calls hit your instance. The bundled alarm buttons always fire payments-service. Catalog and evidence lookups expect the sample URL layout under /services/, /runbooks/, and /incidents/. The three registered actions are simulated in-process, and the acting user is asserted rather than authenticated.
takeItFurther: Persist incidents and the audit log. An audit log you can lose by restarting a process is not an audit log.
Add the rest of the dashboard: response-time rollups, an expiring-soon lane, and an end-of-shift handoff summary.
Replace the simulated actions with real governed tools, keeping the registry boundary and the approval log exactly where they are.
Write the postmortem draft back into your knowledge base. The next incident then retrieves it as precedent, and the evidence rules get better over time.
Expose the copilot over Agent-to-Agent (A2A) so another agent can request triage, with the same approval gate in front of every action. See https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/a2a-client.

guardrails.title: Relevance is not evidence
guardrails.rule: Only a matching past incident may support a causal claim. Runbooks support procedures, not causes.

limitations.title: Authorization is not authentication
limitations.description: Live and fixture both restrict who may approve, but they trust the asserted actor (INCIDENT_ACTOR or, in demo mode, X-Incident-Actor). A deployment must authenticate the actor and decide which credential executes actions. This recipe reports impersonation: false.
